summary: Successive observations of the presence of a ball in the sky: lack of information.
description: A brief and recent account (August 28, 2009) of an old observation. During 1965 or 1966, probably in August (the witness remains vague about the date), several people observed, on consecutive mornings, a stationary ball of metallic brilliance in the eastern sky near a chimney being demolished. No sound was heard during the observations of this phenomenon, which eventually disappeared. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a stationary and bright triangular object in the sky: probable observation of a scientific balloon.
description: Recent report of an old observation made on July 23, 1965, around 6:00 PM. A metallic-looking, triangular object was stationary in the sky and strongly reflected sunlight. This case of observation by multiple witnesses of a luminous object fixed in the evening sky has all the characteristics of a stratospheric weather balloon. The luminous, metallic appearance is characteristic, the apparent immobility is not uncommon, their very high altitude (up to 40 km) makes their movements apparently very slow, and the winds at this altitude are highly variable. The altitude calculation made by the witness is accurate; it is consistent with this hypothesis of a weather balloon that reflected sunlight until 40 minutes after sunset. The planet Venus was clearly visible that evening, shining brightly in the west shortly after sunset. It is surprising that the witnesses did not mention it; but it was much further west and lower than the observed phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a stratospheric balloon.

summary: Sighting of an unknown craft and close encounter; traces on the ground: unidentified phenomenon.
description: On July 1, 1965, at 5:45 a.m., a farmer in his lavender field heard a whistling sound that intrigued him. He went to investigate and found a dark, matte object, unfamiliar to him, on the ground. He observed two figures for four to five minutes before they quickly climbed back into the craft. It took off and flew off at an angle before rapidly disappearing in the direction of Manosque. About ten minutes later, the farmer discovered marks on the ground where the craft had been: these marks were star-shaped with a cylindrical hole in the center, in the sodden earth. He returned that evening around 8:30 p.m. with his daughter and noticed that the ground had become "as hard as cement." The next morning, July 2, he spoke of the incident, and very quickly, many curious onlookers gathered to see the marks, which were then trampled. Around 7:30 p.m., the local gendarmerie learned of the event through word of mouth. The witness was first interviewed on July 2, 1965, at 8:00 PM by the local police station (see report 445). Around 10:00 PM, the witness accompanied the gendarmes to the scene. He was interviewed again from 11:15 PM to 11:30 PM for further information. A report of findings at the observation site and on the traces on the ground was drawn up on July 3 by another police station (see report 105), including measurements and photographs. The witness provided very detailed additional information on August 18, 1965 (see report 145). No other witness statements were collected. No other clues were found around the observation site by the gendarmerie. At the time of this observation, GEPAN, created in 1977, did not yet exist. The successive heads of GEPAN/SEPRA/GEIPAN were all certainly interested in this case, received or collected documents on the subject, without, however, publishing a thorough investigation; a GEPAN investigation would probably have been of little use due to the time elapsed since the event, and after the investigative work already carried out by the Gendarmerie and by several investigators, including Pierre Guerin and Jacques Vallée. Given its unusual nature, this case is classified as D e.

summary: Very brief and recent testimony (2009) of an old observation (early July 1965); observation from a "children's" vehicle emerging from an object shaped like an upturned plate in a lavender field: lack of information.
description: Recent testimony (August 17, 2009) of an earlier sighting made at the beginning of July 1965 (the witness does not specify the exact date; an arbitrary date of July 1, 1965, is given; the witness also does not specify the exact location of the sighting). In a brief email, a witness reports a sighting made from a vehicle on an unspecified road between Moustiers-Sainte-Marie (04) and Manosque (04): around 7:00 or 7:30 PM, during a trip through the Verdon Gorge and while crossing a lavender field, the witness, then 14 years old, and his 4-year-old brother saw from the back of the car "a large overturned plate in a field" and "children coming out of this plate." No further information was gathered, and no other testimony was reported. This seemingly strange case is too poorly documented for an investigation (no precise location or date). The additional information requested by GEIPAN has not been provided. This case is classified as "C," making investigation impossible. However, the position of the moon at its rising in the southeast on July 11th could be a cause for misinterpretation. This obviously does not explain the small beings (children?) observed.
